## Goal

Define a release gate that distinguishes constitutional architecture, completed formal coverage, and a claim of full constitutional conformance.

The framework is ratified at the first dedicated stage of the approved 0.3.0 work, before dependent implementation. The initial ratification is an affirmative act of the natural-human project maintainer adopting the exact constitutional text for edition 2026, with the adopting authority, text identity, and effective date recorded. Appointment of the Constitution Guardian Office is a separate recorded act; initial ratification does not depend on an already constituted Office.

The later 0.3.0 release gate verifies that ratification and the applicable implementation, proof-status, compatibility, and release requirements have been satisfied. v1.0.0 requires full discharge over the current admitted scope. Neither milestone freezes one theorem type or one acceptance relation.

## 0.3.0 readiness

### Normative coverage

Every public language construct must be specified by the Reference or explicitly marked experimental and excluded from the stated compatibility/certification scope.

Implementation behavior cannot silently become normative merely because tests pass.

### Production boundary

All public certified program and realization paths must reach the production acceptance boundary in #136. Frontends, providers, compatibility paths, backends and exporters must not create a second acceptance authority.

Specify what connects source claims to the checked representation and what connects target claims to actual emitted artifacts and evidence.

### Jurisdiction and Constitution Guardian Office coverage

Every semantic feature has a disposition under Soundness, PR and RS through #140. Existing interpretations may cover routine changes; new constitutional cases and disputes are subject to the Constitution Guardian Office's final interpretation.

A feature absent from historical ledger entries is still subject to the three current jurisdictions.

### Proof status and ledger

Record:

- current formalizations and their actual verified scope;
- binding interpretations and outstanding obligations;
- discharged ledger entries and the guarantees they preserve;
- semantic transport and current acceptance/artifact bindings;
- unproved or provisional claims.

Pre-v1 development does not require all three complete production proofs, but it must not claim completed constitutional certification beyond the actual coverage. A pending obligation or passing test is not a discharged theorem.

Already discharged guarantees remain binding before v1.0.0 as well as after it.

### Conformance and compatibility

Use positive/negative conformance evidence and QLT/corpus regression for specification agreement and the published compatibility policy.

Acceptance shrinkage may violate compatibility even if it preserves the safety implication. Keep this gate separate from constitutional safety proof coverage.

### Constitutional CI

The release commit/artifacts must pass #141's applicable text-identity, ledger-continuity, production-binding, proof-status and proof-replay checks. No review marker may waive an applicable ledger guarantee.

## v1.0.0 and later full-conformance gate

A release claiming full constitutional conformance must:

1. discharge all three jurisdictions over its current accepted language and accepted target realizations;
2. re-discharge all applicable historical ledger guarantees against the current production acceptance and current artifacts;
3. justify semantic transport where definitions/representations differ;
4. make its proof boundary and assumptions explicit;
5. satisfy the separate published compatibility/release policy.

If proof coverage is missing, the affected feature/realization cannot be admitted with the corresponding certification. Restrict acceptance or complete the proof; do not relabel an unproved case as verified.

Formal realizations may continue to strengthen after v1.0.0 within edition 2026.

## Suggested 0.3.0 checklist

```text
[x] exact constitutional text affirmatively ratified by the natural-human project maintainer for edition 2026, with text identity, adopting authority, and effective date recorded
[ ] authority model established and Constitution Guardian Office appointment separately recorded
[ ] current production boundary and source/artifact connections specified
[ ] all three jurisdictions documented
[ ] binding interpretations and ledger status recorded
[ ] public constructs covered by the Reference
[ ] theorem-impact analysis and actual proof coverage published
[ ] provisional/unproved claims explicitly distinguished from certification
[ ] no certified path bypasses current acceptance
[ ] constitutional CI and compatibility checks pass
```

## Non-goals

This issue does not require completing all three proofs in 0.3.0, freezing future theorem syntax, guaranteeing compatibility with every later pre-v1 release, or completing later tooling milestones early.

It does require truthful release claims and preservation of guarantees already discharged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Define separate 0.3.0 architecture/readiness and v1 full-conformance gates.
- [ ] Require normative coverage and current production-boundary coverage.
- [ ] Require jurisdiction impact and binding interpretation records.
- [ ] Publish pending versus discharged status and actual certification scope.
- [ ] Preserve already discharged ledger guarantees throughout the pre-v1 period.
- [ ] Require current-scope proofs and historical ledger replay for full conformance.
- [ ] Bind proofs to actual release artifacts and justified semantic transport.
- [ ] Keep compatibility/corpus regression as an explicit separate gate.
- [ ] Require constitutional CI on the release.
- [ ] Remove the former v1 theorem-statement-freeze requirement.

## Core principle

> **Ratification establishes the obligations; release claims state what is proved; full conformance requires the current implementation to discharge every applicable obligation.**


### Draft 5 / Article IX release-gate synchronization

For releases before v1.0.0:

- any same-edition change to ratified `CONSTITUTION.md` must either be absent or be a valid Article IX rectification;
- the rectification must be affirmatively authorized by the natural-human holder or human members of the Constitution Guardian Office;
- the record must explain why the change repairs logic, semantics, formalization, consistency, or textual expression without changing adopted policy;
- no discharged guarantee may be weakened or withdrawn;
- artificial intelligence, autonomous agents, software systems, or analogous non-human entities may not supply constitutional authorization.

After v1.0.0, Article IX no longer authorizes same-edition constitutional rectification.

### Dependency outline and decision packets

1. **Ratification and minimum enforcement first (G01, G03).** Make the exact text and adoption record reviewable, obtain affirmative human ratification, record the distinct Guardian appointment, and activate text-identity protection. Draft preparation is permitted before ratification; dependent language implementation is not.
2. **Binding interpretations and production identity (G02).** Establish the authority hierarchy, pending/discharged ledger representation, current acceptance and artifact binding, and theorem-impact process. Engineering proposals do not become binding constitutional interpretations merely by being included in this plan.
3. **Core semantic and architectural decisions (G04, G05, G10, G11).** Resolve the common type/effect/operator/Meaning model, including #83's operator-interface decision, before implementing dependent specializations. Audit primitive versus derived source; define canonical symbol, qrate, edition, checker, and release identity. Design one shared frontend at this stage rather than extending the two frontends independently.
4. **Static and operational implementation (G05, G06, G07).** Implement bounded static evaluation, kinds, constraints and capabilities, then the jointly specified access/lifetime/control rules. Resolve shared failure/effect questions as one packet. Prove structured clean discharge and compatible-access commutation against the actual admitted definitions before relying on them. Retain deterministic source evaluation.
5. **Canonical language and corpus cutover (G08, with G04–G07, G10, G11).** Implement one grammar, AST, resolver, checker, diagnostics path and CLI. Complete the construct/option migration map, migrate stdlib/examples/both corpora, and compare small-system complex amplitudes and instruments with the fixed historical oracles. Do not preserve a second legacy acceptance path.
6. **Realization and resource contracts (G09).** Build on G02 and the semantics fixed in G04–G07. Keep semantic validity separate from target support; bind target claims to closed implementations, workspace, layout, phase, approximation contracts and provider identity. The explicitly later concrete capability schema in #179 and full theorem milestones are not silently pulled into 0.3.0 or used to defer the current abstract obligations.
7. **Documentation and diagnostics throughout (G12, G13).** Each packet supplies normative rules, source-local diagnostics, positive and negative examples, and source-preservation evidence as its implementation lands. The Guide explains these rules without creating them. Final documentation and diagnostics closure follows the completed cutover and contract work.
8. **Final release readiness (G03).** All 13 groups feed the release gate. Re-run the applicable proof/audit, conformance, corpus, package, installation and distribution checks on the actual release candidate; record performed/skipped results and exact artifact/checker identity. Ratification is verified here, not postponed until this stage. Tagging and publication remain separate actions.

The groups assign primary tracking responsibility, not an instruction to finish every item in one group before starting any other group. Cross-group prerequisite decisions are recorded explicitly; only independent work proceeds in parallel.

### Evidence required to close work

Keep decisions, status, and blockers in the linked issues. For each implemented packet, record the applicable normative decision, actual implementation/acceptance path, proofs and their assumptions, source/artifact bindings, migration, positive and negative conformance cases, and performed validation. A passing test is not a proof; a proved IR property alone is not source preservation; a ratification or interpretation record is not formal discharge.

Use the existing authoring-session procedure for first sources, real diagnostics and counterexamples. Validate small quantum systems and preserve exact phase, axis order, ownership shape and arbitrary-reference behavior where the contract requires them. Do not generate maximum-size cases for this work.

The acceptance criteria above and in each linked issue remain authoritative for issue completion. The tracker does not waive existing guarantees, certify pending obligations, or authorize unrelated future work.

## Executable scoped release-readiness gate contract — 2026-10-05

Implement this ordinary release-tooling unit under the adopted 0.3.0 plan and this issue's existing scoped-release rule. It adds no constitutional interpretation, guarantee admission, tag or publication authorization.

**Problem and result.** The current `check_constitution.py --require-release-ready` unconditionally rejects and mentions the three broader pending obligations as a blocker. Replace that placeholder with an executable, fail-closed readiness gate. A truthful scoped 0.3.0 candidate may retain the broader QS/PR/RS pending obligations. It must still satisfy every applicable 0.3.0 acceptance criterion and preserve all admitted guarantees. Source-only constitutional validation, closed Issue counts, and an arbitrary JSON `passed` field do not establish release readiness.

**Verification inputs.** Keep GitHub as the sole decisions/progress ledger. A candidate may contain an acceptance-evidence index, not a second backlog: the exact 110 selected Issue IDs and 13 groups from the maintainer-corrected tracker (all original 108 plus #311 and #315), each adopted criterion's Issue/snapshot reference and digest, implementation/Reference/migration/positive-and-negative evidence references, and its reviewed disposition. Missing or unresolved criteria fail. The index cannot invent blanket waivers, silently reduce criteria, or move work to later releases; only the already explicit later-version boundaries recorded in the Issues are eligible exclusions. Do not manufacture a completed real index while the implementation remains incomplete. Human specification review remains distinct from mechanical evidence validation; a hashed Issue snapshot does not authenticate human adequacy.

Keep generated verification receipts outside the candidate commit to avoid self-referential commit hashes. Bind the exact candidate commit/tree, product version, edition 2026, schema/profile identities, CI run/attempt, validation selection/results and actual planned artifact bytes separately. The trusted base and trusted hosted-job context are supplied by the caller/workflow, not chosen by candidate JSON. JSON must not supply arbitrary executable commands. Use fixed registered validators, reject unknown/duplicate fields and identities, and recheck mutable inputs after verification.

**Checks.** Require (1) a clean candidate identity and version synchronization, without dependency updates; (2) complete acceptance-evidence coverage; (3) ratified text/adoption identity, trusted-base guarantee continuity and actual current Lean verifier replay; (4) full validation profile AND full proof lane, with all eight required suites successful for the same commit/run/attempt; (5) successful package/source/fresh-install records and the exact expected native assets, each matching its source commit and actual bytes; (6) truthful pending-versus-admitted proof scope, production-path and migration coverage. Preserve edition, release, qrate schema, native protocol and artifact identity as separate concepts. Frontend edition validation alone cannot satisfy the outstanding effective-edition-to-native-acceptance criterion.

**CI placement and provenance.** Remove the release check from inside `check-docs`; a readiness job must run after the real validation suites, avoiding a circular dependency. Reuse the existing required-suite aggregation and add release-specific full-lane checks. Run the release gate for tags and an explicit manual readiness request; ordinary development PRs/full validation do not require all 110 issues to be finished. Receipts saved on failure are diagnostic artifacts, never proof of success. Consumers must compare actual downloaded bytes with producer digests carried by trusted same-run job outputs and check run/attempt/commit identities. Merely hashing an offline report does not authenticate GitHub CI provenance.

The legacy `--require-release-ready` entry point must delegate to this gate or reject missing required context clearly; it must never succeed from source-only checks. Existing non-release constitutional checks retain their purpose. Keep all current real missing acceptance evidence as a failure with actionable diagnostics.

**Required regression evidence.** Reject missing/duplicate Issue IDs, criterion removal, unauthorized exclusions, stale/missing evidence, a different commit or merge commit, tests/model proof lanes, skipped/cancelled/missing suites, failure-created receipts, wrong run/attempt/digest, source-only proof validation, admitted-guarantee removal, fabricated discharge, mismatched asset bytes/source/version, missing expected assets and changed inputs during checking. Include a complete small synthetic positive candidate that truthfully retains the three broader pending obligations and preserves/replays the two admitted scoped guarantees; fixture success is not actual repository readiness. Exercise CLI delegation and workflow placement/provenance, not only internal schema helpers.

Publication readback remains a distinct later action: tag peel, downloaded GitHub/registry assets and installed artifacts must match the checked candidate after separately authorized publication. This unit neither publishes nor calls a candidate “published”, and does not claim final readiness for the current unfinished tree.


## Distribution scratch lifecycle correction — 2026-10-05

Disk inspection found retained local validation trees, including five Cargo target subtrees per distribution run; `check_distribution.py` creates a new persistent artifact directory on every invocation and never removes owned build scratch. This is a resource-management defect in repeated release validation, not evidence that corpus probes generate unbounded files. At inspection, local `/private/tmp/qleisli-*` entries totalled about 92.7 GiB by du, including historical outputs and APFS shared blocks; this is not a predicted reclaim amount.

**Implementation contract:** keep the report, command logs, exact crate and source archive as durable validation evidence. Put internally owned extracted source trees, installation and default Cargo targets in a separate temporary work directory, and clean it on success and failure after recording useful diagnostics. Add an explicit `--keep-work` debugging option; never delete a caller-owned external `--target-dir`. Report work-directory identity and retention/cleanup status truthfully. Cleanup failure must not be labelled as success or hide the original validation failure. Do not weaken any package, source, installation, proof or release check. Existing large historical paths are not deleted automatically by this code change.

**Validation:** use small synthetic command drivers to verify success/failure cleanup, explicit retention, preservation of external target sentinels, durable evidence and truthful cleanup errors; run the existing distribution validator tests. No fresh multi-GB build is needed for this lifecycle unit. Full real distribution validation remains required on the final integrated candidate. This correction adds no release approval or new guarantee admission.
